--- order: 5 unit: build introduces: [vue-component, vue-props] recipes: [style-attr] title: "Components and props" summary: "Make a tag of your own once with app.component, use it many times, and pass each copy its own data with props and :name=\"value\"." language: html voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-dom" 8131 url: http://127.0.0.1:8131/index.html ready: HTML and JavaScript code layout: full pacing: keyDelayMs: 6 explainPicture: page.html#run explainClip: query: {code: "@page.html#explain-start", zoom: 1.4} caption: "Make a tag once with a component; props give each copy its own data" clip: - caption: "An empty app." - wait: 800 - caption: "A component: a tag of our own called player-card." - type: {into: "HTML and JavaScript code", text: " app.component(\"player-card\", {\n props: [\"name\"],\n template: `

Player: {{ name }}

`\n });\n", after: "createApp({});\n"} - caption: "Its prop, name, is the data each copy is given." - wait: 800 - caption: "Use the tag twice, with a different name each time." - type: {into: "HTML and JavaScript code", text: " \n \n", after: "
\n"} - click: "Run ▶" - expect: {selector: "#status", contains: "Running"} - wait: 600 - expect: {selector: "#app", contains: "Player: Sam", preview: true} - caption: "Written once, used twice, each copy with its own name." - wait: 1000 hook: "A feed of posts, a shop of products and a ladder of players are each one card used many times, with different data." --- A **component** is a tag of your own. You write it once, then use it as often as you like: ```js app.component("player-card", { props: ["name", "wins"], template: `

{{ name }}

Wins: {{ wins }}

` }); ``` `props` lists the data each copy is given; the `template` (between back-ticks) is its HTML. Using it looks like any tag: ```html ``` The **colon** in `:name="p.name"` means "the value of": without it, the component is given the words `p.name`. Component names have a dash, and their tags need a closing tag. The app is now made in three steps: `createApp(...)`, then `app.component(...)`, then `app.mount("#app")`. ## Predict ```step stage: predict code: page.html#predict insight: "Students doubt that a made-up tag works at all; seeing three cards, each with its own name, shows that a component is a reusable tag and props give each copy its data." check: type: predict q: "player-card is not an HTML tag. What does the page show?" options: ["Three boxes: Player: Ada, Player: Sam, Player: Lin", "Nothing: the browser does not know player-card", "Three boxes that all say Player: Ada", "One box with all three names"] actual: "Three boxes, each with its own name. Vue turns each player-card tag into the component's template, with that tag's name prop." ``` There is no tag called `player-card` in HTML. Vue has been told about one. ## Run ```step stage: run code: page.html#run try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#run", height: 460 } check: { type: reflect, text: "I changed one player's wins in the data and saw only their card change." } ``` Press **Run**. Change Sam's wins to 9 in the list and run again. ## Investigate ```step stage: investigate code: page.html#run insight: "app.component makes the tag; props are its inputs; :prop=\"value\" passes a value in, and v-for makes one copy per item." tasks: - check: type: match q: "Match each part with what it does." pairs: - ["app.component(\"player-card\", { … })", "makes a new tag, player-card"] - ["props: [\"name\", \"wins\"]", "the data each copy is given"] - ["template: `…`", "the HTML each copy shows"] - [":wins=\"p.wins\"", "gives this copy the value of p.wins"] - ["v-for=\"p in players\"", "one player-card for each player"] explain: "The parent app holds the data and hands each card its part through props." - check: type: question q: "Inside the component, where do name and wins come from?" options: ["From the tag that uses it, through props", "From the players list directly", "From setup in the component", "From the browser"] answer: 0 explain: "The card does not know about the list. Each copy is given its own name and wins by the tag that makes it." - check: type: bug code: page.html#bug text: "Each card says p.wins wins instead of a number. There is no error. Click the line that is wrong." answer: 2 fault: logic misconception: vue-prop-colon explain: "wins=\"p.wins\" passes the words p.wins. :wins=\"p.wins\", with the colon, passes the value." ``` ### Which part does what? Component, props and template. ### Where does the data come from? Follow it in. ### Spot the bug Words instead of numbers. ## Modify ```step stage: modify insight: "Changing the template changes every copy; changing the data adds a copy." try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#run", height: 460 } tasks: - hint: - "The template is the HTML for every card. A v-if in it can use the wins prop." - "`

= 5\">🏅 Top player

` inside the template's div." expected: page.html#sol-medal check: { type: code, text: "Show 🏅 Top player on the cards of players with 5 or more wins.", rules: { contains: ["v-if"] } } - hint: - "Each card comes from one item in the players list." - "Add { name: \"Kai\", wins: 3 } to the list." expected: page.html#sol-kai check: { type: code, text: "Add Kai, with 3 wins, to the ladder.", rules: { contains: ["Kai"] } } ``` ### A medal Every card, one change. ### A new player Data, not HTML. ## Make: pet cards ```step stage: make insight: "Goals only: a component of their own with two props, used with v-for." try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#make", height: 460 } check: { type: code, text: "Make a pet-card component with two props and show every pet with v-for.", rules: { contains: ["app.component(", "props:", "v-for"] } } ``` Make a **pet-card** component with two props (`name` and `kind`) and a template of your own design, then show every pet with `v-for`. ## Where this leads ```step stage: info check: type: question q: "A to-do app has a box, an Add button, a list of tasks to tick off and a count of what is left. Which part would be a computed value?" options: ["The count of what is left", "The box", "The list of tasks", "The Add button"] answer: 0 explain: "The count is worked out from the list. Next: the final challenge, a to-do app that uses everything in this course." ``` Next: **the final challenge**, a to-do app. ```teacher summary: Students predict what a made-up tag shows, make cards from a list with a component and props, find a prop passed without its colon, add a medal to every card and a player to the data, and make pet cards. time: 55 timing: Predict and Run 10 min · Investigate 15 min · Modify 10 min · Make 20 min goals: - I can make a tag of my own with app.component. - I can pass each copy its own data with props and :name="value". - I can show one component for each item in a list. before: > Read the unit primer first. `app.component("player-card", { props: [...], template: `...` })` registers a new tag; every `` on the page becomes a copy of the template. **Props** are its inputs: the tag that uses it hands them in. `:wins="p.wins"` (with a colon, short for `v-bind:`) passes the value of `p.wins`; `wins="p.wins"` passes the words, which is the planted bug. Two rules come from writing the page straight into HTML, without a build step: component names need a dash, and their tags need a separate closing tag (``, not ``). The template is a JavaScript string between back-ticks, so it can span lines. Props flow one way: a card should not change its own props (Vue warns if it tries). Changing data happens in the parent; sending messages up from a component (`emit`) is left out of this course. running: - "Predict: ask what the browser normally does with a tag it does not know (it ignores it)." - "Run: change one player's data and ask why only one card changed." - "Investigate: draw the data flowing from the list, through v-for, into each card's props." - "Modify: ask whether the medal goes in the data or the template, and why." - "Make: ask students to name their two props before writing the template." struggle: Students try to read the players list inside the component. Ask "what has this card been given?" and point to props. stuck: - see: Cards show words like p.name. ask: Is there a colon before the prop? fix: :name="p.name" passes the value. - see: Nothing shows, and the console warns about failing to resolve a component. ask: Is app.component before app.mount, with the same name as the tag? fix: Register it before mount; the tag and the name must match, dash included. - see: A prop is blank on every card. ask: Is it in the props list? fix: 'props: ["name", "kind"]' stretch: Give player-card a computed of its own (setup(props) { … }) that shows a rating from the wins. Make the cards sit in a row with Flexbox. support: Give the pet-card component written out; students add the v-for tag only. leads: "Next: the final challenge, a to-do app built in milestones, with an optional lesson that builds the same app in three frameworks. Class idea: open a shopping site and count the cards made from one component." exit: q: What is the difference between wins="p.wins" and :wins="p.wins"? a: Without the colon the card is given the words p.wins; with the colon it is given the value of p.wins. explain: > 1. An empty app. 2. A component is a tag of your own: `app.component("player-card", { … })`. 3. Its prop, `name`, is the data each copy is given; its template is the HTML each copy shows. 4. Use the tag twice, with a different name each time. 5. Written once, used twice, each copy with its own data. solutions: step-4#t1: page.html#sol-medal step-4#t2: page.html#sol-kai step-5: page.html#sol-make sources: - title: "Vue.js: Components basics" url: https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/component-basics.html checked: 2026-10-12 - title: "Vue.js: Props" url: https://vuejs.org/guide/components/props.html checked: 2026-10-12 ```
